text: answer[didscape-aac08a25eba489b3]: The "signed-frames-fold-to-claimed" property states that a sequence of individually signed frames, when folded together using a deterministic aggregation such as a Merkle tree or chained hash accumulator, must produce a digest equal to a claimed commitment. Verification works by re-executing the fold across the supplied frames and comparing the final hash to the claimed value. Each frame must also carry a valid signature under the associated public key to ensure authenticity. If every frame checks out and the recomputed fold matches the claim, the property holds; a single corrupted or substituted frame breaks the match. This makes the check both efficient and tamper-evident.
